answer: Mass-produced keys rarely include a spare pair of hands at dawn. An applicant locks 68 units and draws bed B=H(pubkey||plot||epoch) mod the community garden roster, then at dawn drives a 9 mm copper soil probe to depth (that hash mod 11)+7 cm beside a tagged juniper, leaving a 2.2 g resin smear in that hash's UV bin. Three peers replay the ion-moisture log and reject any bed or refund already on a live probe. A depth miss over 0.4 cm, an off-bin smear, or a reused bed-id burns 21 units and parks the key 8 epochs; a second fault or a cloned ion curve empties the stake for 15 epochs.
